$comment: B5 runtime vs incumbent (D-20260929-b5-runtime-ratchets): one downward-only ratchet per (package, incumbent) pair, ours ÷ theirs in-process. `ceiling` is what benchmarks/axes/runtime.ts gates each pair on; `target` is the bar every pair is held to in the end, at or below the incumbent. `history` is append-only and never rises: scripts/runtime-ratchets-lock.test.ts refuses a `ceiling` that is not the last entry, an entry above the one before it unless it cites a newer decision in .sdlc/decisions/, a history that rewrites the committed one, and a pair the axis measures with no ratchet (or a ratchet for no pair). A PR that makes a pair faster appends a lower step in the same commit; `npm run ratchets:propose` prints how far each can come down from the CI observations on main.

derive.rule: The largest median `runtime-ratio` of the last 10 CI observations in benchmarks/results/cli-benchmarks/*-ci.json (or the PR run that lowers it, cited in the step), times 1.25 for a shared runner's noise on an in-process ratio, rounded up to the next 0.05. Target 1.0: at or below the incumbent.

history.why: First ceiling, deliberately generous: 1.5x the 8.221 measured on a loaded laptop (load 40-60) at 9d35a82, because no CI run had measured B5 yet. The PR that introduces the axis lowers it from its own CI run.

derive.rule: bellpull R8's bar, not a derived ceiling: spawn time at or under tinyexec, so the ceiling IS the target and never rises above it. The derive rule the other pairs use (the largest median of the last 10 CI observations times 1.25) would put it above 1.0 and turn R8 into a ratchet it never asked to be. It may still come down: the largest median of the last 10 CI observations times 1.25, rounded up to the next 0.05, once that is under 1.0.

history.why: R8's bar, set at the target on the first step: bellpull ÷ tinyexec read 0.922, 0.932, 0.933, 0.940 and 0.949 across five runs on an M4 Pro at load 55-60 (median 0.933), so the pair is under 1.0 before any ceiling is derived for it. Gating at the bar rather than at 1.25x a measurement keeps R8 a requirement instead of a ratchet that starts above it.
